SOC-F01.name: Normative Climate & Informal Enforcement
SOC-F01.landscape: Constructs, mechanisms, measures, theories, interventions, outcomes, moderators, identification problems and controversies reviewed once at Family level.
SOC-F01.principalBoundary: actual descriptive/injunctive norms, perceived norms, norm messages, expectations and sanctions remain distinct

scientificLandscape.constructs: descriptive and injunctive norms, visibility, consensus, sanctions and rewards
scientificLandscape.mechanisms: expectation formation, conformity incentives and informal enforcement
scientificLandscape.measures: behavior prevalence, expressed approval and actor-specific norm perception must be labeled separately
scientificLandscape.operations: norm feedback, peer-behavior claims and sanction/reward cues
scientificLandscape.outcomes: belief, intention, observed behavior and norm change require distinct endpoints
scientificLandscape.moderators: referent proximity, baseline behavior, credibility, privacy and setting
scientificLandscape.identification: norm messages often bundle comparison, credible source, reward and prompts
scientificLandscape.controversies: actual norms cannot be recovered from perceived norms or message content alone

SOC-F02.name: Direct Social Influence Conditions
SOC-F02.landscape: Constructs, mechanisms, measures, theories, interventions, outcomes, moderators, identification problems and controversies reviewed once at Family level.
SOC-F02.principalBoundary: peer presence, model similarity/status, exposure and influence require identification beyond observed similarity

scientificLandscape.constructs: peer presence, model similarity/status, majority signal, unanimity and minority consistency
scientificLandscape.mechanisms: informational and normative influence, modeling and conformity
scientificLandscape.measures: assigned peer exposure must be separated from endogenous peer similarity
scientificLandscape.operations: peer assignment, endorsement, modeling and majority/minority displays
scientificLandscape.outcomes: task choice, attitude and behavior are not generic influence
scientificLandscape.moderators: publicness, task ambiguity, model status and group identification
scientificLandscape.identification: reflection, homophily, shared context and simultaneity
scientificLandscape.controversies: similarity and adjacency do not identify contagion

SOC-F03.name: Interaction & Relational Embeddedness
SOC-F03.landscape: Constructs, mechanisms, measures, theories, interventions, outcomes, moderators, identification problems and controversies reviewed once at Family level.
SOC-F03.principalBoundary: contact frequency, duration, reciprocity, multiplexity, closeness, tie survival and tie formation are not interchangeable

scientificLandscape.constructs: interaction frequency/duration, reciprocity, multiplexity, closeness, tie age, formation and dissolution
scientificLandscape.mechanisms: repeated interaction, exchange, opportunity and relational investment
scientificLandscape.measures: event rates, tie reports and closeness scales use different units
scientificLandscape.operations: contact assignment, repeated interaction and bounded link revision
scientificLandscape.outcomes: tie formation, survival and closeness require temporal ordering
scientificLandscape.moderators: tie type, relationship stage, setting and observation window
scientificLandscape.identification: selection into interaction and endogenous tie retention
scientificLandscape.controversies: contact quantity is not relationship quality

SOC-F04.name: Inclusion, Support & Social Integration
SOC-F04.landscape: Constructs, mechanisms, measures, theories, interventions, outcomes, moderators, identification problems and controversies reviewed once at Family level.
SOC-F04.principalBoundary: available, received, perceived and enacted support remain distinct from network size, integration and loneliness

scientificLandscape.constructs: inclusion, ostracism, available/received support, integration, isolation and network size
scientificLandscape.mechanisms: resource access, belonging, stress buffering and exclusion
scientificLandscape.measures: objective contact, received support, perceived support and loneliness are non-equivalent
scientificLandscape.operations: support provision, mentoring, group access and exclusion tasks
scientificLandscape.outcomes: support receipt, integration and psychological belonging remain separate
scientificLandscape.moderators: need, provider fit, relationship quality, age and clinical status
scientificLandscape.controversies: larger networks need not provide better or received support

SOC-F05.name: Cooperation, Reciprocity & Mutual Dependence
SOC-F05.landscape: Constructs, mechanisms, measures, theories, interventions, outcomes, moderators, identification problems and controversies reviewed once at Family level.
SOC-F05.principalBoundary: cooperation, intention, trust, reciprocity expectation, observed reciprocity and prevalence remain separate levels

scientificLandscape.constructs: cooperation, free riding, reliability, reciprocity, mutual aid and resource sharing
scientificLandscape.mechanisms: repeated games, conditional cooperation, reputation and interdependence
scientificLandscape.measures: laboratory contributions differ from population prevalence and generalized cooperation
scientificLandscape.operations: public-goods structures, reputation feedback, sanctions and repeated interaction
scientificLandscape.outcomes: choice, intention, prevalence and collective result must be separated
scientificLandscape.moderators: stakes, anonymity, repetition, partner matching and group size
scientificLandscape.identification: game structure and observability components are often bundled
scientificLandscape.controversies: task cooperation does not establish a stable social preference

SOC-F06.name: Status, Reputation & Relational Power
SOC-F06.landscape: Constructs, mechanisms, measures, theories, interventions, outcomes, moderators, identification problems and controversies reviewed once at Family level.
SOC-F06.principalBoundary: formal authority, informal status, prestige, dominance, reputation, centrality and resource control remain distinct

scientificLandscape.constructs: rank, mobility, reputation, deference, authority, resource control and dependence asymmetry
scientificLandscape.mechanisms: status allocation, control dependence and reputational inference
scientificLandscape.measures: rank nominations, resource distributions and network centrality capture different properties
scientificLandscape.operations: reputation displays, role assignment and resource-control changes
scientificLandscape.outcomes: deference, influence and legitimacy require separate evidence
scientificLandscape.moderators: formal role, task domain, visibility and group hierarchy
scientificLandscape.identification: status both shapes and results from interaction
scientificLandscape.controversies: centrality, prestige, dominance and authority are not interchangeable

SOC-F07.name: Network Structure & Position
SOC-F07.landscape: Constructs, mechanisms, measures, theories, interventions, outcomes, moderators, identification problems and controversies reviewed once at Family level.
SOC-F07.principalBoundary: network metrics are boundary-dependent calculations, not autonomous causal agents or adjacency state

scientificLandscape.constructs: degree, betweenness, closeness, eigenvector centrality, density, clustering, assortativity, constraint, segregation, centralization and fragmentation
scientificLandscape.mechanisms: network state constrains paths and opportunities; metrics summarize the bound state
scientificLandscape.measures: node set, tie type, direction, weight, boundary, window, variant and normalization are mandatory
scientificLandscape.operations: seeding, tie/node changes, rewiring and boundary changes
scientificLandscape.outcomes: state deltas and metric recalculation are not empirical effects
scientificLandscape.moderators: network boundary, missingness, multiplexity and exposure mapping
scientificLandscape.identification: endogenous formation, interference, reflection and metric constituent reuse
scientificLandscape.controversies: derived metrics may predict outcomes without being autonomous causes

SOC-F08.name: Network Exposure & Social Diffusion
SOC-F08.landscape: Constructs, mechanisms, measures, theories, interventions, outcomes, moderators, identification problems and controversies reviewed once at Family level.
SOC-F08.principalBoundary: reach, tie, transmission, exposure, attention, acceptance and retransmission are successive non-equivalent states

scientificLandscape.constructs: network exposure, cross-cluster exposure, source count, frequency, reinforcement and retransmission
scientificLandscape.mechanisms: simple/complex diffusion, redundant exposure and threshold processes
scientificLandscape.measures: potential reach, receipt, attention, adoption and retransmission require separate mappings
scientificLandscape.operations: network seeding, nominated referents and repeated peer exposure
scientificLandscape.outcomes: adoption and diffusion are content- and behavior-specific
scientificLandscape.moderators: topology, threshold, source dependence, timing and content
scientificLandscape.controversies: network exposure is not ordinary independent-unit treatment

SOC-F09.name: Group Composition, Cohesion & Deliberation
SOC-F09.landscape: Constructs, mechanisms, measures, theories, interventions, outcomes, moderators, identification problems and controversies reviewed once at Family level.
SOC-F09.principalBoundary: composition, diversity, cohesion, deliberation, participation equality, conflict and performance require separate measures

scientificLandscape.constructs: group size, cohesion, diversity, fractionalization, participation equality, dissent and information coverage
scientificLandscape.mechanisms: information pooling, identification, conflict and workflow coordination
scientificLandscape.measures: composition indices, process observations and cohesion scales are distinct
scientificLandscape.operations: group assignment, deliberation protocol and structured discussion
scientificLandscape.outcomes: performance, consensus, polarization and cooperation are separate
scientificLandscape.moderators: task type, tenure, workflow intensity and facilitation
scientificLandscape.identification: composition is not randomized in most teams and processes can mediate reciprocally
scientificLandscape.controversies: density, cohesion, consensus and performance cannot substitute for one another

SOC-F10.name: Coordination, Accountability & Collective Capacity
SOC-F10.landscape: Constructs, mechanisms, measures, theories, interventions, outcomes, moderators, identification problems and controversies reviewed once at Family level.
SOC-F10.principalBoundary: coordination opportunity, behavior, efficacy belief, capability, accountability and outcome remain distinct

scientificLandscape.constructs: interdependence, goal/expectation alignment, common knowledge, accountability, role clarity and collective efficacy
scientificLandscape.mechanisms: mutual predictability, monitoring, coordination and shared-goal pursuit
scientificLandscape.measures: belief in capacity differs from resources, observed coordination and outcome
scientificLandscape.operations: accountability cues, coordination protocols, shared goals and role assignment
scientificLandscape.outcomes: participation threshold, contribution and collective performance
scientificLandscape.moderators: task coupling, group size, communication and authority
scientificLandscape.identification: successful outcomes can cause efficacy reports and obscure coordination process
scientificLandscape.controversies: collective efficacy is not objective collective capacity

SOC-F11.name: Audience & Social Evaluation
SOC-F11.landscape: Constructs, mechanisms, measures, theories, interventions, outcomes, moderators, identification problems and controversies reviewed once at Family level.
SOC-F11.principalBoundary: audience presence, size, identifiability, publicness, monitoring and evaluation exposure are separate manipulations

scientificLandscape.constructs: audience presence/size, identifiability, publicness, evaluation exposure and monitoring
scientificLandscape.mechanisms: reputation concern, evaluation apprehension and accountability
scientificLandscape.measures: observability of actor, action, outcome and history must be specified
scientificLandscape.operations: public commitment, audience manipulation, identity display and monitoring cues
scientificLandscape.outcomes: self-presentation, task behavior and population prevalence remain distinct
scientificLandscape.moderators: anonymity, audience relevance, stakes and prior reputation
scientificLandscape.identification: identity and reputation information are often bundled
scientificLandscape.controversies: audience presence does not guarantee evaluation or sanction

SOC-F12.name: Intergroup Contact, Boundaries & Competition
SOC-F12.landscape: Constructs, mechanisms, measures, theories, interventions, outcomes, moderators, identification problems and controversies reviewed once at Family level.
SOC-F12.principalBoundary: contact quantity, quality, friendship, cooperation, status equality, boundary permeability and hostility are distinct

scientificLandscape.constructs: contact frequency/quality, cross-group friendship, cooperation, competition, hostility, status inequality and boundaries
scientificLandscape.mechanisms: learning, anxiety reduction, recategorization, threat and resource competition
scientificLandscape.measures: contact quantity, valence, intimacy, group status and attitude targets must be explicit
scientificLandscape.operations: structured contact, cooperative tasks and competition structures
scientificLandscape.outcomes: attitude, prejudice, friendship and institutional integration are distinct
scientificLandscape.moderators: equal status, common goals, support, voluntariness, valence and group position
scientificLandscape.identification: self-selection into contact and wide intervention heterogeneity
scientificLandscape.controversies: negative contact may outweigh positive contact and optimal conditions operate as a package
